To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CKI(delta) is a key kinase in the Xenopus circadian clock.
two Xenopus casein kinase I isoforms (full-length and deletion CKI(delta)) are expressed in the frog retina, and that both isoforms are localized to photoreceptor nuclei.

two isoforms of Xenopus casein kinase I, CKI(delta) full-length and CKI( epsilon), have been isolated and shown to be constituitively expressed in the Xenopus photoreceptor cells where the circadian clock is localized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the circadian rhythm in Xenopus laevus.
the molecular mechanisms underlying circadian clock function.
the role of CKI(delta), CKI(epsilon), and CKI(delta) in the regulation of the retinal clock.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CKI(epsilon)/CKI(delta) are involved in the regulation of the circadian clock in the frog retina, and that this role is conserved in evolution.

CKI(delta) plays an important role in the retinal circadian oscillator in Xenopus laevi s, and that the CKI(delta) full-length isoform, and not the CKI(delta )deletion isoform, is involved in PER phosphorylation, and possibly degradation.

CKI(delta) is a nuclear localized protein kinase that is capable of phosphorylating and degrading PER in the nucleus, and that the deletion isoform of CKI(delta), lacking the nuclear localization signal and the two protein kinase domains, is not involved in the regulation of the circadian clock.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CKI(delta) full length and CKI(eps) isoforms are involved in the retinal circadian clock, and the CKI(delta), deletion isoform is not involved.
we have identified and characterized several isoforms of CKI in Xenopus and shown that they are expressed in the retina, where the circadian clock has also been localized.

we have identified a CKI(delta) that is a candidate for the CKI that degrades Drosophila and Xenopus PER, but that the deletion CKI delta does not have the necessary features for degradation of PER, and that the CKI(epsilon), which has been shown to be involved in degradation of mammalian PER, is not involved in the Xenopus clock.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified the first casein kinase I delta isoform from the Xenopus lae vis species and that this kinase is involved in the regulation of PER protein.
CKIs are involved in retinal circadian clocks, and that CKIs may be involved in the degradation of PER.
the Xenopus laeavis retina is an ideal system to investigate the molecular mechanism underlying the retinal circadian clock.
